behavioral_notes.observation: Publishing is the core side-effect. write() stamps published_date with now() the first time is_published/website_published flips on (if not already set), and archiving a post (active=False) force-sets is_published=False. On both create() and write(), _check_for_publication() fires for any active post being published and calls blog_id.message_post_with_source('website_blog.blog_post_template_new_post', subtype='website_blog.mt_blog_blog_published') -- i.e. publishing a post posts a 'new post' announcement on the parent blog's mail.thread, notifying its followers. None of this state-machine/notification logic is visible in metadata.

blog.post inherits website.seo.metadata + website.published.multi.mixin and overrides _default_website_meta() to emit OpenGraph/Twitter-card tags: og:type='article', article:published_time=post_date, article:modified_time=write_date, article:tag=tag names, plus og:image extracted from cover_properties background-image, og:title/og:description from name/subtitle. The teaser field is computed (first 200 chars of content stripped of HTML) or overridden by teaser_manual. website_url is computed as /blog/<blog-slug>/<post-slug> via ir.http._slug. SEO/meta generation lives entirely in Python.

The /blog/<blog>/<post> route (controllers/main.py) increments blog.post.visits once per visitor session: it checks request.session['posts_viewed'] and, if the post id is absent, calls sql.increment_fields_skiplock(blog_post,'visits') (an atomic UPDATE that skips row locks) then records the id in the session. The same controller computes next_post for sequential navigation and renders 'website_blog.blog_post_complete'. Visit counting is a raw-SQL session-gated side-effect, invisible to ORM metadata.

Reader comments are mail.thread messages: blog.post sets _mail_post_access='read' (any user with read access may post a comment) and website_message_ids is filtered to message_type='comment'. The controller paginates comments at _post_comment_per_page=10. _notify_thread_by_inbox is overridden to suppress inbox/needaction notifications for 'comment' messages (emails only), and blog.blog.message_post downgrades replies on the 'Presentation Published' email to internal notes (subtype mail.mt_note) to avoid spamming all blog followers. Comment plumbing reuses the mail stack, not a dedicated model.

15 JS files, 5 XML templates, 0 OWL components; behavior ships as website 'public.interactions' (blog_posts, blog_post_link, website_blog) plus edit/preview interaction variants, and two builder patches (CoverPropertiesOption.prototype, NewContentSystrayItem.prototype) for the cover editor and the 'New Blog Post' systray entry. Asset bundles span web.assets_frontend (3), website.assets_editor (1), website.website_builder_assets (1). The s_blog_posts dynamic snippet renders posts inside the page builder.

it_architecture.application: website_blog (Blog application component on the website front end)
information_flows: side-effect: blog.post publish (is_published) -> blog.blog.message_post_with_source('blog_post_template_new_post', subtype mt_blog_blog_published) notifies blog followers
side-effect: blog.post publish -> stamps published_date = now(); archive -> is_published = False
side-effect: reader comment -> mail.message (message_type=comment) on blog.post via mail.thread; inbox notifications suppressed for comments
side-effect: blog.post._default_website_meta -> OpenGraph/Twitter article meta tags for SEO/social sharing

external_integrations.notes: No outbound HTTP / SDK / API-key usage in code (http_call_sites=0, uses_api_keys=false). The only endpoint is the product page https://www.odoo.com/app/blog declared in __manifest__.py. Social reach is achieved passively via OpenGraph/Twitter-card meta tags and an Atom feed (/blog/<blog>/feed), not an outbound social/marketing API.

capabilities: Manage Content SEO & Social Sharing (meta/OpenGraph, sitemap, Atom feed)
Measure Reach (per-post visit counts, follower announcements)
value_streams: Content-to-Audience: draft post -> tag & set cover/SEO -> publish (announce to blog followers) -> visitors read (tracked visits) -> readers comment (mail.thread) -> attract/engage audience

Unpublished posts / future post_date hidden unless user is website.group_website_designer
blog.post._mail_post_access='read': any read-access user may post a comment
stakeholders: Content editor / author (res.users in website.group_website_designer; res.partner author_id)
metrics: publish announcements to blog followers (engagement proxy)

classification.apqc_category: 3.0 Market and Sell Products and Services
classification.rationale: website_blog is a value-network mediating activity (Stabell & Fjeldstad): it publishes content to attract and engage an audience, brokering the relationship between the organization and its readership through mediating infrastructure -- public blog pages, tag-based navigation, SEO/OpenGraph metadata, an Atom feed, visit tracking, follower announcements on publish, and a reader-comment channel (mail.thread). Per Stabell & Fjeldstad the network firm's primary activities are network promotion & contract management and service provisioning; content marketing recruits and serves an audience network rather than transforming inputs (chain) or solving a bespoke client problem (shop). It is a primary marketing activity -- the inbound content-marketing channel, not internal support -- mapping to APQC 3.0 Market and Sell, specifically 3.3 Develop and manage marketing plans and 3.4 Develop and manage marketing communications (publishing marketing/editorial content and measuring its reach).
